title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the ps1 wrapper keeps '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, so its own bare `& git` and its worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs can run a project git.exe (ps1 twin of task-0b2ea570)
description:
Found while planning task-52555102 (prototype and logs in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/52555102-plan).

Measured on 2026-11-03 on this Windows host, with PS 5.1 and PS 7:
- With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 and a '.' entry first on PATH, a protected governor launch of moe-agent.ps1 runs a <project>\git.exe planted at the project root. The wrapper's own PowerShell `& git` calls run it, not the agent Git guard.
- PowerShell walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries. Find-MoeProtectedFile skips them only for node and the agent CLI, and $env:PATH is left as inherited.

Two more wrapper Node programs spawn git by bare name with no cwd option:
- Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch's `git` helper: scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~:3260, sh twin prepare_worktree_launch ~:3394.
- Invoke-MoeBoardSnapshot: ~:7345, sh twin board_snapshot ~:7858.

On Node 22+ (libuv 1.48+), the NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 that task-2f22237b exports already stops the implicit current-directory lookup (mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first, re-measured 2026-11-03). Two gaps remain:
- libuv still walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries.
- Node 20 and older ignore the variable.
task-0b2ea570 covers the sh wrapper's PATH and moe-call.sh; this row is the ps1 twin.

Fix direction:
- Under the marker, rewrite $env:PATH once, early (right after the marker is read and before any bare-name call), to the absolute entries outside the project that Find-MoeProtectedFile accepts.
- And/or pass task-52555102's trusted git path to the worktree-launch and board-snapshot programs. Keep both wrappers' program texts identical, as their twin tests require.
- Mirror whatever design task-0b2ea570 lands for sh.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, a git.exe planted at the project root and reachable through a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry never runs during a protected governor launch of moe-agent.ps1. The check is the whole exe log, not only the agent Git guard's children. A protected-agent-command row run through Windows node.exe proves it for PS 5.1 and PS 7.
Under the marker, the worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs never spawn git by bare name, in either twin. A test row or a mutant-checked assertion pins this.
Legacy seats are unchanged. parity-check.sh, the protected-agent-command and agent-git-guard suites, and the launcher suites exit 0 on Linux and through Windows node.exe.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1: PATH scrub under the marker, with the WT-13 check moved after it. This is the twin of sh protected_scrub_path (task-0b2ea570). Edit with the Edit tool only, and keep the UTF-8 BOM and LF-only endings.

(a) Give Find-MoeProtectedFile (:570) a list mode instead of copying its per-entry test. This follows the architect comment on this row: the scrub and every lookup share ONE definition of 'outside the project', the one from task-89579137 (see mem:gotcha-windows-final-path-canonicalization and mem:gotcha-windows-subst-ancestor-walk).
- An empty -Name collects every entry that passes the existing checks. Those checks are: absolute; its real path is neither the project nor under it; and on Windows its final path is local and not under the project key.
- Collect each entry's UNTRIMMED real path ($realFull) and return the list in PATH order. Do not use the trimmed $real: a root entry trimmed to 'C:' would become drive-relative.
- The named mode keeps its first-hit return.
- Error handling stays as it is. The per-entry try/catch skips an unreadable entry. A project that cannot be placed prints the one [WARN] line and returns nothing.
- Leave every other task-89579137 byte unchanged.

(b) Add the scrub under $script:MoeRuntimeProtected, after Resolve-MoeProtectedCli is defined and before `$script:MoeNode = $null` (the node pin).
- Compute `$moeTrusted = @(Find-MoeProtectedFile '' @() | Where-Object { $_ })`. Filter, because a function that returns $null yields one $null element.
- If the list is empty, call Stop-MoeProtectedAgent with the existing node line, verbatim: '[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: node was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start.' Add no new MOE_ code, and never set PATH to '': in PowerShell that deletes the variable (mem:gotcha-powershell-empty-env-var-deletes).
- Otherwise set `$env:PATH = $moeTrusted -join [IO.Path]::PathSeparator`.
- A hot-reload pass reruns this on a PATH that is already scrubbed. It must leave that PATH unchanged (idempotent).

(c) WT-13: turn the `$moeInWorktree = & { ... }` block (:145) and its refusal (:168) into a function with the same body.
- Keep the local `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'`, the catch that returns $false, the MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER -cne '1' seam, and the same stderr line with `exit 1`.
- At the function's current spot, call it only when `$env:MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED -cne '1'`. $script:MoeRuntimeProtected is not defined yet at that point. This keeps legacy order and output unchanged.
- Under the marker, call it right after the scrub, so its three `& git` calls resolve from the scrubbed PATH.
- Add a comment that under the marker no bare-name command may run before the scrub. A grep of :120-616 finds no other native command today.

The Windows tests in steps 3-4 cover this.

implementationPlan.description:
Both wrappers: under the marker, the worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs spawn only an absolute git.

(a) Programs. Make the same edit in both copies, so each pair stays byte-identical and ASCII. postflight-worktree.cjs boardJs() already asserts the board pair, and X1 in step 4 asserts both pairs.
- The tooling programs are ps1 Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch :3327 and sh worktree_tooling_node :3461.
- The board programs are ps1 Invoke-MoeBoardSnapshot :7408 and sh board_snapshot_node :7928.
- Reuse the agent Git guard's idiom from task-52555102: `const strict = process.env.MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED === '1', GIT = strict ? process.env.MOE_PROTECTED_GIT || '' : 'git';`
- In each git helper, before spawning, add `if (strict && !path.isAbsolute(GIT)) throw Error(...)` with a message that names MOE_PROTECTED_GIT. Then spawn GIT instead of 'git'.
- Add a one-line comment that cites task-3acf7f79 and says why: Node looks a bare name up in the cwd (Node < 22) and in '.', relative and in-project PATH entries. See mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first.

Error handling: each helper's first call already sits inside its program's try, so a refusal takes the existing failure path.
- The tooling program exits 1 with the message as its last line, which the wrapper reports as MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- The board program prints [WARN] MOE_BOARD_SNAPSHOT_SKIPPED and exits 0, so the landing is unaffected.
- Keep the argv layout (argv.slice(-4) and argv.slice(-3)) and every other byte. postflight-worktree.cjs runs both programs directly, with a legacy env.

(b) Export MOE_PROTECTED_GIT under the marker.
- ps1: inside the node-pin block, after Set-Alias, set `$env:MOE_PROTECTED_GIT = Find-MoeProtectedFile 'git' <@('.exe') on Windows, @('') on POSIX>`. A missing git assigns $null, which deletes the variable, so the programs fail closed.
- sh: in protected_pin_interpreters, after PYTHON_CMD, add `MOE_PROTECTED_GIT=$(protected_path_lookup git "$project" .exe) || MOE_PROTECTED_GIT=""` and then `export MOE_PROTECTED_GIT`. This form is set -e safe.
- Legacy never sets the variable, and the programs ignore it there.
- Leave the guard's own lookups ($guardGit and guard_git) unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Pass git to the two programs as an extra argv, like the guard does. Rejected: it changes argv.slice(-4) and argv.slice(-3), which postflight-worktree.cjs's direct runs (projectYml, boardJs) depend on. An env var (MOE_PROTECTED_GIT) leaves the argv alone.
2. Rely on the ps1 PATH scrub alone for the programs. Rejected: Node < 22 still searches the cwd (the project) first on Windows, and DoD 2 forbids any bare-name spawn under the marker.
3. Move the marker and the protected helpers above WT-13. Rejected: they need $projectPath, which resolves at :435 and can come from a -ProjectName registry lookup. Deferring WT-13 under the marker is smaller and keeps legacy identical.
4. Copy Find-MoeProtectedFile's per-entry test into the scrub. Rejected: two definitions drift. A list mode (empty -Name) shares the one from task-89579137 and keeps the named mode's first-hit return.
5. Refuse the launch up front when no trusted git exists. Not needed: the guard already refuses any CLI launch with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED, and the programs fail closed.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The ps1 hot-reload supervisor reruns the whole file in the same process, so $env:PATH carries over between passes and the scrub must be idempotent.
- PowerShell walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, but never the cwd implicitly. cmd.exe and Node 22+ skip the cwd under NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath, and every libuv still walks '.' and relative entries.
- Under the marker, both .NET process starts (Start-Process at :977 and ProcessStartInfo at :10167) use the pinned $script:MoeNode.
- In sh, PATH is already scrubbed at :81 and :142 (task-0b2ea570). The only remaining sh gap is the programs' bare 'git' under DoD 2.
- The tooling pair (4465 chars) is identical today, but only the board pair is asserted identical (postflight-worktree.cjs boardJs). X1 adds the tooling assertion.
- protected-agent-command's run() clears MOE_* and sets MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER=1, so its rows never reach the WT-13 refusal. The worktree-harness wt-guard case covers that refusal, which is why both the sh and the ps1 wt-guard are in the gate.
planningNotes.risks:
- `@(f)` on a function that returns $null gives a one-element array, so filter with Where-Object.
- Use the untrimmed real path: 'C:' is drive-relative.
- `$env:PATH = ''` deletes the variable, so refuse before it.
- Precedence under the marker changes only in which refusal comes first: the command refusal now precedes WT-13. Both still come before any side effect.
- Network or UNC PATH entries are dropped under the marker on Windows, consistent with task-89579137 (fail closed).
- Git Bash: MOE_PROTECTED_GIT reaches native node.exe only through MSYS env conversion, and the suite skips sh-on-Windows. If the path is unconverted, /mingw64/... spawns ENOENT, and the programs fail closed (mem:gotcha-msys-argv-posix-path-conversion-launcher-tests).
- Performance: list mode resolves every PATH entry once per pass (on PS 5.1, roughly 0.1-0.3 s). The named lookups still stop at their first hit.
- Plant only git.exe in W3. PS 5.1 resolves a git.ps1 before git.exe in the same dir (mem:gotcha-git-shim-windows-powershell), and a .ps1 is invisible to the node logger, so the legacy non-vacuity leg would go blind.
- X1 (c) needs a git identity for commit-tree.
- Windows rows need a normal WSL shell for the node.exe leg: under env -i, interop loses git.
- The ps1 worktree leg needs a D: temp dir.
